- `action/knowledge-audit.sh` runs `hermes -z` (one prompt in, the final answer out) with the provider, model and, for a custom endpoint, the base URL from its environment, and the API key from a secret the caller names. Nothing in the script names a vendor; Ollama, OpenAI, Bifrost and OpenRouter are examples in the docs.
- Read only (I2): the run enables only Hermes' file-read and search tools, with no terminal, write, patch, web or code-execution tool, and refuses to start otherwise. Measured on main: audit mode accepts 1 provider (Anthropic, through `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), and the shipped workflow shows 0 of the commands it runs.

# audit-any-provider

Relayed from: operator, 2026-10-15: "Use hermes instead, and let it take any provider e.g. OLLAMA, OPENAI, brifrost etc." and, for the workflow, explicit steps over a hidden `uses:`.

## Intent

The audit mode added by ci-audit runs `claude -p` and needs an Anthropic API key. The operator does not want either. It changes to [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com), which talks to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

- `action/knowledge-audit.sh` runs `hermes -z` (one prompt in, the final answer out) with the provider, model and, for a custom endpoint, the base URL from its environment, and the API key from a secret the caller names. Nothing in the script names a vendor; Ollama, OpenAI, Bifrost and OpenRouter are examples in the docs.
- Read only (I2): the run enables only Hermes' file-read and search tools, with no terminal, write, patch, web or code-execution tool, and refuses to start otherwise. The prompt carries the audit skill, the review skill for each batch and the `kmctl-auditor` instructions as text, since Hermes does not load Claude Code agents.
- The token rules from ci-audit-hardening stay: no GitHub token reachable from the model's step, checkout without persisted credentials, and a separate issue step.
- `.github/workflows/knowledge-audit.yml` spells out each step (install kmctl, install Hermes, write its config, run the audit script, post the issue) instead of `uses: ./`, so a reader sees every command. `action.yml` keeps the same steps for callers who prefer `uses:`, with `provider`, `model`, `base_url` and `api_key_env` inputs in place of `anthropic_api_key`.
- A new decision record says why: the audit must not tie a repository to one model vendor. It names what it replaces (the Claude Code runner from ci-audit) and links ADR 0005. The how-to, the architecture overview and ADR 0005's Consequences follow.

Measured on main: audit mode accepts 1 provider (Anthropic, through `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), and the shipped workflow shows 0 of the commands it runs.

Done when the tests run the audit script with a stub `hermes` and show the provider, model and base URL reach it from the environment, the toolsets it enables are only the read ones, the prompt holds the skill and auditor text, and the findings still reach the summary and the issue body; the shipped workflow's steps name every command; and a spike shows real Hermes, pointed at an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, offers the model no write or terminal tool with those settings and returns a findings block the script parses.

## Could invalidate this plan

- Hermes may have no way to enable file reading and search without also enabling writes or a terminal, which would break I2. Spike it against a fake OpenAI-compatible endpoint that records the tools Hermes offers.
- `hermes -z` may not run unattended in CI (an approval prompt, a setup wizard, a config it insists on), or may not take the provider and base URL without a config file. Spike the same run with a fresh `HOME`.
